item.text: The campaign is live in the US with an $87.50 daily budget and a $700 lifetime cap, ending at midnight after Halloween in Denver. I chose the two posts that explain the show and its free listening options, so people know what they’re clicking through to.
The first day spent $77.43 for 32 link clicks. Both posts performed similarly, but the click rate was low, so I’ve narrowed the audience to US horror and thriller fans to improve relevance.

The narrower audience raised cost per click, so I’ve restored broad US targeting and added your approved “mine shaft breathe” post as another creative. Reported totals are now $170.45 and 52 link clicks; figures have also updated since the first check.
Yesterday’s creative results were close: roughly $2.56–$2.65 per link click across all three posts. There isn’t a clear winner yet, so I’m keeping delivery steady while more results accumulate.

At the halfway point, reported spend is $342.71 for 287,514 impressions and 122 link clicks. I’ve set a $2 target bid to try to improve click efficiency; I’ll check whether it affects delivery tomorrow.

The target bid brought yesterday’s reported cost to about $2 per link click: $61.94 for 31 clicks. I’m keeping it and allowing up to $100 per day over the final three days, with the $700 lifetime cap still in place.
With two days remaining, the campaign has reported $480.71 in spend, 429,631 impressions, and 191 link clicks. Delivery is continuing within budget; I’m retaining the current bid through the weekend.
Halloween starts with $560.66 spent and 231 link clicks reported. I’ve made the remaining budget available for today, retaining the $2 target bid and the midnight Denver end time.
The campaign has ended at midnight Denver time and is paused. I’m allowing one hour for reporting to catch up before pulling the recap.
